notes: Prompt delivery is STDIN via `codex exec -` (documented: with `-` the full prompt is read from stdin). All modes pair the sandbox with --ask-for-approval never, because a bridge job cannot answer approval prompts. accept-edits uses --sandbox workspace-write explicitly; the deprecated --full-auto shortcut is NOT used. auto maps to danger-full-access + never - that is no sandbox at all; it exists so the common scale is complete, and your mode ceiling keeps it off unless you deliberately raise or remove the ceiling (the shipped example config sets readonly, and the job must declare the mode explicitly either way). NEVER emitted: --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox / --yolo (the runner's denylist also blocks them). Status is community, not verified, for two honest reasons: (1) Codex parses -c values as TOML, so the effort value is emitted as a quoted string (model_reasoning_effort="high") per vendor guidance, but the literal composed form has not been confirmed against a live binary's `codex exec --help`; (2) the composed argv places the stdin sentinel `exec -` before the sandbox/approval flags, and no captured help output settles flag position for every build. The effort allowlist (minimal..xhigh) follows the cited config reference; some models accept additional levels (max, ultra) - those are deliberately not allowed here. Confirm both points on your install and this adapter can be promoted to verified. Config surface: config.toml / project .codex configuration and MCP servers in the job's environment apply to bridge jobs and are NOT bounded by the job's mode - see SECURITY.md.
